name: Common Valerian
family: Caprifoliaceae, the honeysuckle family (formerly the valerian family, Valerianaceae)
grown_as: A native perennial wild flower of damp grassland and stream banks, also grown as a herb and pollinator plant
habit: An upright plant 1 to 1.5 m tall, from a short rootstock. Stems grooved, hollow, little branched below the flower heads. Leaves in opposite pairs.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite pairs up the stem; larger leaves from the base
leaf.type: Compound, once pinnate, with 7 to 25 leaflets
leaf.leaflets: Narrow lance-shaped, 3 to 8 cm, stalkless; the end leaflet like the side ones
leaf.base: Leaflets narrowing to the midrib, the bases running along it a little
leaf.margin: Irregularly toothed or almost untoothed, often a few coarse teeth on each side
leaf.veins: A midrib and faint side veins
leaf.surface: Hairless above, a little hairy beneath
leaf.stalk: Long on basal leaves; short or none on stem leaves

flower.form: Tiny funnel-shaped flowers massed into rounded domed clusters
flower.petals: Joined into a small tube with five spreading, slightly unequal lobes; the tube a little swollen at the base
flower.centre: Three stamens sticking out beyond the lobes
flower.behind: Calyx rolled inwards and hidden at flowering
flower.carried: In branched rounded clusters at the top of the stem, upright; sweet scent
flower.size: Each flower 3 to 5 mm; clusters 5 to 10 cm

fruit: Small oblong flattened seeds 2.5 to 5 mm, each topped with a feathery white parachute (the calyx unrolled)
seedling: Two small rounded seed leaves, then first true leaves simple and oval, later pinnate
winter: Dies down to a small rosette or bare crown; dead hollow stems may stand

leaf: once pinnate with many narrow lance-shaped leaflets
leaves in opposite pairs on the stem
bloom: rounded cluster of tiny tubular five-lobed flowers
seed: small flat seed with a feathery white parachute
seedling: first true leaf simple and oval
young: basal leaves pinnate with narrow leaflets
flower: tall stem with opposite pinnate leaves
rounded pale pink flower clusters at the top
seedhead: clusters of seeds with feathery parachutes
dormant: small low rosette or bare crown

look_alikes: Red valerian (Centranthus ruber) has undivided grey-green leaves and red, pink or white spurred flowers. Hemp-agrimony has leaves of three to five lobes and pink fuzzy flowers. Marsh valerian is smaller with undivided basal leaves.
